comparison: Both strongly support pH-dependent polymorph selection (C3, C24, C26, C27, C32). OpenEval emphasizes systematic cryo-EM structural analysis and pH thresholds. Peer review highlights all three reviewers' explicit affirmation and describes findings as 'important' with 'strong support for pronounced sensitivity to environmental conditions.' Peer review additionally includes C7 (overall synthesis claim).

Both support cross-seeding findings showing pH dominates over seed structure (C4, C54-C59, C64). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from ThT kinetics, cryo-EM, and LiP-MS data. Peer review (R3 statement) explicitly endorses 'non-polymorph-specific seeding in secondary nucleation-dominated aggregation' and notes editor's recognition of buffer condition dependence. Peer review additionally includes C65 (mechanistic framework).

Both support discovery of disease-relevant JOS-like polymorph (C5, C29). OpenEval focuses on cryo-EM structural data and backbone conformation similarity. Peer review emphasizes this as a key discovery with editor and reviewers highlighting 'possibility of in vitro reconstruction of brain-derived structures' and mentions phosphate ion hypothesis. Peer review additionally includes Type 1 meta-analysis claims (C37-C39).

Both support novel Type 5 polymorph discovery (C6, C30, C31, C49, C51-C53). OpenEval emphasizes unique structural features from cryo-EM and notes appropriate acknowledgment of rarity. Peer review explicitly highlights this as one of 'two new polymorphs' of particular note, with structural characterization and disease relevance. Peer review additionally includes C50 and C69 (structural relationships to other polymorphs).

Perfect agreement on Type 2 and 3 polymorph structural analysis (C25, C40-C42, C45-C47). OpenEval details tertiary/quaternary structural differences and E46K mutant findings. Peer review confirms 'high-resolution structures enable clear characterization' and describes evidence as convincing with appropriate structural detail. Both evaluations fully aligned.

Perfect agreement on pH 7.0 variability and polymorph diversity (C33-C36). OpenEval emphasizes extensive cryo-EM analysis across ten samples and buffer-dependent differences as important findings highlighting shallow energy landscape. Peer review confirms these observations are part of systematic study that reviewers found convincing, supporting overall environmental sensitivity conclusions.

Perfect agreement on subtle symmetry differences between Type 3B structures (C43-C44). OpenEval notes small but documented differences suggesting seeding condition influences. Peer review confirms this structural observation with cryo-EM data is not challenged and represents technical detail supporting broader structural characterization.

Both support mechanistic hypothesis for pH-dependence (C28). OpenEval notes C28 as 'reasonable mechanistic hypothesis' though speculative. Peer review confirms this speculation is presented tentatively and not challenged, representing reasonable hypothesis based on pH-dependent observations reviewers found convincing.

Both support thermodynamic interpretation of pH 6.5 polymorph coexistence (C48). OpenEval finds interpretation consistent with data. Peer review confirms inference presented with appropriate uncertainty, supported by citations, and aligns with overall pH-dependent findings that reviewers strongly support.

Both address Type 1 polymorph analysis (C37-C39). OpenEval provides comprehensive meta-analysis from literature with buffer-dependent K58 orientation supporting shallow energy landscape concept. Peer review groups these claims with JOS-like polymorph discovery (C5, C29), emphasizing disease relevance and in vitro reconstruction possibility.

Both support amyloid growth mechanism framework (C60-C63, C66). OpenEval synthesizes established knowledge with authors' findings, noting mechanistic framework explains pH-dependent selection. Peer review confirms these established concepts provide context for experimental findings, with explicit endorsement of secondary nucleation conclusions. OpenEval additionally includes C65.

Peer review groups C50 and C69 with broader Type 5 discovery (C6, C30-C31, C49, C51-C53), emphasizing resemblance to patient-derived structures.
